question: A capillary blood glucose reading of 198 mg/dL obtained 2 hours after a meal in a symptomatic patient is diagnostic of diabetes mellitus on its own.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The random glucose threshold for diagnosis with symptoms is ≥200 mg/dL. A value of 198 mg/dL falls just below that threshold and does not meet diagnostic criteria on its own.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. A 2-hour post-meal (postprandial) capillary glucose of 198 mg/dL does NOT meet the diagnostic threshold of ≥200 mg/dL. Diagnosis requires ≥200 mg/dL with symptoms, or confirmation by a second test.
